The package's ambient declarations are listed explicitly: `@wing-agent/ui` is source-first, so its `.d.ts` files are only in a consumer's program if the consumer includes them (imports do not pull ambient declarations in). `types: [vite/client]` keeps node globals out — `process`/`Buffer`/`require` are compile errors here, so nothing embedded in the document can depend on the extension host's environment. `vscode` is not in the type set either (and lint/tests ban the import). The renderer itself (`@wing-agent/ui`) is type-checked through this program too: it resolves to source (`exports` → `src/index.ts`), which is exactly what the bundlers consume.
